title: Anchored at a Cove With No Name
coverImageAlt: Placeholder — real photo of the unnamed cove to come
excerpt: We found it by accident three seasons ago and have gone back more times than we can count since.
subtitle: Some of the best anchorages in the bay never made it onto a chart with a name attached.
author: Thibault Poirson
body:
It doesn't have an official name, at least not one we've found on a chart, so the crew just calls it the cove. It's a fifteen-minute detour off the standard route between La Paz and Espíritu Santo, and most charters never stop there because it's not on anyone's list.

We found it three seasons ago on a day when the wind pushed us further off our planned line than expected, and it's been a regular stop ever since, mostly for the color of the water at the right angle of afternoon light.

> Half of running expeditions here without a fixed schedule is being willing to stop somewhere just because it looks right that day.

![Boat placeholder — real photo of the boat at anchor to come](/assets/img/boat-baydreamer-exterior.webp "The boat at anchor, mid-afternoon, cove unnamed.")

There's nothing built there and nothing particularly rare about it by Baja standards; it's a beach and clear water like several others nearby. It just happens to be quiet in a way that's hard to find anywhere with a name.

We don't publish the coordinates. Not out of secrecy exactly, more because half the appeal is that it isn't a planned stop, and we'd rather it stayed that way.
